idiom: by the skin of one's teeth
meaning: only just managing to do something, with a very narrow margin
example: We finished the project by the skin of our teeth, just before the deadline.
origin: Possibly from the Bible (Job 19:20), meaning to escape with only the thinnest margin; the exact wording and meaning are disputed.

wrong_meanings.meaning: to lose all of one's teeth
wrong_meanings.why_wrong: This is a literal misreading of the words; the idiom is figurative and is about a narrow success or escape.

wrong_meanings.meaning: to have a very clean and healthy body
wrong_meanings.why_wrong: The idiom has nothing to do with health or hygiene; it describes a very close result.

wrong_meanings.meaning: to be extremely generous with money
wrong_meanings.why_wrong: The idiom describes a narrow margin of success, not generosity or spending habits.

explanation: 'By the skin of one's teeth' means only just managing to do something, with very little to spare. It is commonly used when someone succeeds or escapes at the last moment.
